- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips from high to low, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid lagged correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict near-term (first 5–7 days) and underpredict later (last 10–15 days); apply downward bias to later days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is uniformly high (e.g., 1.00 for 3+ days), model often fails to account for mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
